scenes.heading: Algebra and pattern problems
scenes.sub: Find the rule, then jump to any term
scenes.say: Matchstick patterns, age riddles, shopping bills — selective algebra questions are about spotting a rule and turning words into maths.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A fence: 10 posts have only 9 gaps between them
scenes.science: From term 1 to term n there are n − 1 jumps
scenes.breaks: fence gaps can be uneven; in a linear pattern every jump is exactly the same size.
scenes.say: Think of a fence. Ten posts have only nine gaps between them. Patterns work the same way: from the first term to the tenth there are nine jumps, not ten. That one idea fixes the most common pattern mistake.
scenes.caption: Think of a fence. 10 posts have only 9 gaps. From the 1st term to the 10th there are 9 jumps, not 10.

scenes.heading: Finding the rule
steps: Start the rule with difference × n
Adjust to hit the first term
scenes.say: To find a rule: find the common difference, start the rule with that number times n, then adjust so it gives the first term. Test it on the second term before you use it.

scenes.heading: Jump to the 20th term
scenes.question: 5, 9, 13, 17, … What is the 20th term?
scenes.say: Five, nine, thirteen, seventeen. The difference is four, so start with four n. Four times one is four, so add one. The rule is four n plus one. The twentieth term is eighty-one.
scenes.caption: 5, 9, 13, 17. The difference is 4, so start with 4n. 4 × 1 = 4, so add 1: the rule is 4n + 1. The 20th term is 81.

scenes.heading: Words to equation
scenes.question: Plumber: $60 call-out plus $45 per hour. Bill $195. How many hours?
scenes.say: A plumber charges sixty dollars plus forty-five dollars an hour, and the bill is one hundred and ninety-five. Sixty plus forty-five h equals one ninety-five. Take away sixty, then divide by forty-five: three hours.
scenes.caption: $60 plus $45 an hour, bill $195. 60 + 45h = 195. Take away 60, then divide by 45: 3 hours.

scenes.heading: Two-bill puzzles
points: Find an item both bills share
Subtract one bill from the other
Work back to the other item
scenes.say: For two-bill puzzles, look for an item both bills have the same number of. Subtract one bill from the other and that item cancels out. Then work back to find the other price.

points: Difference first, then fix the start
scenes.say: Quick recap. Find the difference first, remember there are n minus one jumps, write one equation with one letter, and always check in the original words. Now try the practice questions!
